sections.heading: DevCon Mumbai / L1 R&D Recap
sections.summary: Three major open questions emerged from DevCon: EIP-8288 forward compatibility, EIP-7906 interaction with paymasters, and SSZ transaction hashing.
sections.body:
- lightclient summarized the Frame Transaction breakout held during DevCon Mumbai (Thursday of DevCon week), highlighting three main outcomes.
- **EIP-8288 forward compatibility:** EIP-8288 proposes aggregating large PQ signatures (and potentially other ZK proofs) into a single block proof. Frames currently use a separate signature list outside the frame list, which is at odds with how 8288 envisions proof handling.
  - lightclient's thinking is trending toward removing the signature list and instead adding a new "PROOF" frame mode where the data can be interpreted by the protocol in the 8288 way.
  - Initially the PROOF frame would contain a regular signature (e.g., ECDSA); in the future it would hold leanSPHINCS or aggregated proofs.
  - The key goal: users should not need to change their wallet again when aggregation ships via 8288.
- **EIP-7906 / paymaster interaction:** With 7906's transaction assertions, paymastered frame transactions face a problem — the ERC20 payment to the paymaster happens after VERIFY ends, but assert can revert execution back to the approval point, potentially reverting the paymaster payment.
  - Several workarounds were explored (e.g., a flag marking a frame as non-revertible by assert); none were satisfying.
  - Allowing some state changes in the verification phase via sender-derived storage rules is a likely path.
  - 7906 may simply not work with paymaster transactions in the public mempool initially.
- **SSZ serialization and hashing:** Etan proposed using SSZ for frame transaction hashing/serialization to get stable container properties and hashtree root benefits across forks.
  - lightclient acknowledged SSZ is better in isolation but noted historical inertia of RLP on the EL and SSZ library concerns, though those arguments are weakening.
  - Justin Florentine (Besu) pushed back, saying SSZ adds scope and doesn't feel compelling for the current timeline.
- lightclient set a one-month window (before end-of-year holidays) to finalize the two larger changes: removing the signature list for 8288 compatibility, and deciding on SSZ serialization.

sections.heading: EIP-8288 Forward Compatibility and Signature Removal
sections.summary: Agreement to pursue a minimal 8288-compatible frame mode for Hegota; Iván (ethrex) to open a draft proposal soon.
sections.body:
- Iván (ethrex) agreed EIP-8288 is too large to implement fully now but advocated splitting it and shipping a minimal first part that is forward-compatible.
  - Plans to open a PR with a draft proposal for a dependency frame supporting only leanSPHINCS initially, to be iterated on in future forks.
- lightclient confirmed: the full 8288 will not be implemented now, but frames should have a mode that represents signatures today and is forward-compatible with 8288.
- Toni Wahrstätter suggested transactions could already ship with a sidecar separating the signature from the transaction body (similar to Bitcoin SegWit), since 8288 with aggregation will require this anyway.
  - lightclient pushed back: no value in separating the signature now since aggregation isn't ready; keep the signature in the transaction and remove it later when needed.
  - Toni accepted keeping signatures inline for now.
- Discussion of signature size without aggregation:
  - lightclient argued Ethereum can function without PQ signature aggregation on the EL — even several hundred transactions with ~4 KB PQ signatures would only add a few megabytes per block.
  - Toni noted aggregation is for efficiency, not safety/security.
  - The CL case is harder (tens of thousands of validators), but EL deals with smaller numbers.
  - Consensus: ship PQ crypto support now; don't block on aggregation.
- lightclient said he needs to study [LeanPCS](https://x.com/VitalikButerin/status/2122233780371083553) more before proposing a concrete design; conversations in Mumbai reduced his confidence that a simple black-box model is sufficient.
  - Justin Florentine (Besu) asked Nico to post LeanPCS resources in ETH R&D; Nico agreed to do so.

sections.heading: leanSPHINCS Precompile vs. EVM Verification
sections.summary: No precompile planned for leanSPHINCS; a formally verified Solidity verifier running in the EVM is the preferred approach if costs are low enough.
sections.body:
- johba shared early experience building a hash-based account for Safe using leanSPHINCS (Nico's optimized variant):
  - Verification in the verify frame costs ~75,000 gas; deploying an account costs ~130K gas.
  - Multisig use cases are blocked by the current 100K MAX_VERIFY_GAS limit.
  - Feedback: fee structure (per gas) differs from spec; signature hash drops signature bytes (not documented clearly); RPC returns a single generic error for all failures.
- Nico confirmed the parameter set johba used is very likely close to the final one; final parameters expected within weeks (deadline of January 2027 for finalized leanSPHINCS).
- Ryan McPeck proposed the ideal flow: 7702 converts EOAs to smart accounts, ecrecover ability is removed, and accounts permanently migrate to frame transactions with new PQ signers.
  - lightclient confirmed this is the current plan.
  - Daniil (Nethermind) noted EIP-8151 is also needed; 8151 exempts 7702 delegation indicators, so plain 7702 leaves old permits alive. [PR #12506](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12506) installs real code, making EIP-3607 kill k1 txs and 8151 kill k1 permits — together they form the full retire path.
- Justin Florentine noted the main argument against a precompile is that it makes zkEVMs more challenging; Sanso preferred running verification in the EVM.
- Nico agreed: if LeanPCS makes verification cheap enough, a precompile can be avoided; a formally verified Solidity verifier would be the reference implementation.
- Rob Dawson asked about a well-known contract; Nico confirmed there would be a formally verified Solidity implementation.

sections.heading: Devnet Prioritization and Scope
sections.summary: Teams should prioritize finalizing spec changes (8288 compatibility, PQ readiness EIPs) over incremental devnet updates in the next month.
sections.body:
- lightclient preferred prioritizing big spec changes over incremental devnet updates, given the volume of spec work needed in the next month.
- Iván (ethrex) advocated freezing the devnet feature set soon to allow thorough edge-case testing, while keeping a window open for the 8288-compatible frame change.
- Toni raised the question of whether a slimmed-down devnet without FOCIL is worth discussing; Iván and Juan Bono from ethrex supported this (+1).
- Guru suggested the immediate priorities should be: frame spec changes, EIP-8151 (restricted ecrecover), and EIP-8298 (SETCODEFROM) — focus on hardening those rather than adding more EIPs.
- spencer stated his personal focus for the next two weeks will be exclusively on frames and PQ specs/tests until ACDE/ACDC clarify whether FOCIL remains in Hegota.
- The broader Hegota scope remains undecided; answers expected from upcoming ACDE (this Thursday) and ACDC calls.

sections.heading: MAX_VERIFY_GAS Increase to 300,000
sections.summary: Nethermind proposed raising MAX_VERIFY_GAS from 100K to 300K based on benchmarks; Besu supportive, but Toni urged caution regarding FOCIL/builder impact.
sections.body:
- Daniil (Nethermind) presented [PR #12644](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12644) to raise MAX_VERIFY_GAS from 100,000 to 300,000, based on benchmarking by their team (Manuel).
  - Initial target was 500K; reduced to 300K to balance functionality (PQ signatures, complex scenarios) with node safety.
- Besu (Justin Florentine) expressed support; encountered the same limits in fuzzing. 300K seemed reasonable but wanted performance team review.
- Toni Wahrstätter cautioned that MAX_VERIFY_GAS affects not just the mempool but also the builder critical path, especially with FOCIL — builders must re-verify frame transactions for inclusion list compliance.
  - Suggested keeping 100K for now but excluding call data cost from the verify gas limit, which would already help significantly with large signatures.
  - Call data is not meaningful computational work for builders, so excluding it from the limit is safe.
  - The right gas limit depends on whether FOCIL ships; may be too early to lock in a number.
- Vansh raised a [concern about MAX_VERIFY_GAS](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/36095#discussion_r4600264115) in a go-ethereum PR.
- Nico noted raising the limit would enable many use cases and advocated pushing even higher if performance allows; mentioned that prior discussions with Soispoke didn't flag FOCIL interaction as a major concern.

sections.heading: Mempool Validation Reference Tests
sections.summary: Mario Vega proposed a new test fixture format for mempool validation rules; client teams gave lukewarm support, and Mario will draft a PR.
sections.body:
- Mario Vega (testing team) proposed creating a new reference test format for mempool validation rules (e.g., max verify gas checks), separate from consensus tests.
  - Would help with regression testing for non-consensus mempool behavior.
  - Described it as a small lift.
- Nethermind (Daniil): "Sounds good."
- Besu (Justin Florentine): interested but wants to think about it more.
- ethrex: lukewarm yes.
- Mario will create a PR for client teams to review and provide feedback.

sections.heading: AA-VOPS Claimed Index and NON_STATE/STATE Verification Split
sections.summary: Justin Zen proposed splitting frame TX verification into NON_STATE and STATE phases to remove the claimed index from AA-VOPS; deferred to async discussion.
sections.body:
- Justin Zen raised [the topic](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2295#issuecomment-6948390788) of removing the claimed index from AA-VOPS (EIP-8369) by splitting verification into NON_STATE (signature/proof, checked once) and STATE (key binding, nonces, payer, re-checked after each append).
  - Problem: EIP-8369 judges omitted frame transactions at a builder-chosen index, so a frame tx is only protected if valid at every index; nonce chains and shared payers can be excused.
  - The index exists because end-of-block re-checks would require replaying the full VERIFY prefix including crypto.
  - Proposed fix: cache the NON_STATE check result when the inclusion list arrives; only re-run the STATE check after each block append, making re-checks as cheap as Profile 1.
- No immediate reactions from client teams; deferred to async discussion.
- Iván (ethrex) and Daniil (Nethermind) acknowledged needing time to review.

sections.heading: leanSPHINCS Bindings Breaking Change
sections.summary: Vansh flagged a breaking change in lean-pq-bindings; implementations should switch to the new PQ bindings.
sections.body:
- Vansh noted that [PR #45 on lean-pq-bindings](https://github.com/ethereum/lean-pq-bindings/pull/45) introduced a breaking change.
- All leanSPHINCS implementations should update to the new bindings.
